concepts.explanation: The person whose inner struggle the story is about. Readers follow this character most closely, and the story asks whether they change.
Whose eyes a scene is seen through. A story can use one or several. It is not always the main character.

The character who presses on the main character's way of seeing things, so the main character has to test it. Related terms a writer may meet: a foil contrasts with the main character; an antagonist opposes the main character's goal. The challenger may be either, or neither.
The outside problem the story is about and what is at stake. Also called the external plot.
The main character's inner change, or refusal to change, as the story goes on. Also called the internal arc.
Whether the main character is a different person by the end or stays the same at heart. Staying firm can be the point of a story.
What the main character is chasing against what they actually need. It often shows up as something they keep doing and must stop, or won't do and must start.
Whether the main character answers trouble by changing the situation or by changing themselves.
Whether the main character works things out step by step or goes with their gut.
Will the main character get what they are after? The ending answers it.
What happens if the main character fails. Without stakes the dramatic question has no weight.
Whether events force the main character to choose, or the main character's choices make events happen.
A story that ends because time runs out, as opposed to one that ends because there is nowhere left to turn.
Whether the main character gets what they were after.
Whether the main character is better or worse off when it is over. With the outcome, it gives the four classic endings: happy, bittersweet, tragic and a hollow win.
What the story is wondering about, for example whether loyalty is worth lying for. The writer's own words; the ending answers it by how it feels.
Whether the challenger comes around to the main character's view or holds to their own by the end.
Whether the main character and the challenger end up closer, broken apart or unsettled.
